A pegasus-flight of three pixel-tall silhouettes crossing the far cloud-bank, their wing-beats lost to distance but their shapes unmistakably horse-winged against the pale sky.
Matchstick-sized deer-herd of perhaps twelve grazing at the forest-edge midground, their tawny forms barely separating from the amber grass behind them.
A lone phoenix soaring at the horizon's upper rim, ant-sized and ember-bright, a single moving spark against the deep violet of the evening sky.
Two unicorn-pair shapes, pinprick-white in a distant sunlit clearing, visible only because the dark tree-wall behind them throws their tiny forms into brief relief.
A wolf-pack of seven matchstick silhouettes moving in single file along the far ridge-line, their shapes merging with the pine-shadow before the crest swallows them entirely.
Ant-sized wild-horses streaming across the open plain midground, perhaps twenty shapes flowing together like a single dark ribbon across the pale winter grass.
A dragon-shadow racing the horizon in deep distance, pixel-tall and unmistakably winged, its moving crescent-darkness briefly darkening a pale strip of river below.
Hippogriff-pair circling in the high thermals overhead, matchstick-sized against the white cloud-belly, their eagle-foreparts and horse-haunches readable only by their silhouette rhythm.
A whale-spout at the far sea-edge, pinprick-white and vertical, lasting three seconds before the ant-sized dark back-curve slides silently below the horizon line.
Firefly-swarm drifting through the twilight meadow midground, their collective glow a faint smear of gold too diffuse to count individual lights at this distance.
A griffon-pair wheeling above the distant cliffside, their ant-sized forms tracing slow opposing circles, visible only when they cross the lighter limestone face.
Matchstick-sized ibex on the far cliff-face, four shapes angled impossibly on vertical rock, their tiny horns catching the late-afternoon sidelight for one brief moment.
A butterfly-cloud lifting from the midground meadow, too distant to distinguish individual wings, the whole swarm reading as a single shimmering pale disturbance in the air.
An aurochs-herd of ant-sized dark blocks moving across the plain deep distance, their mass suggesting weight and number though each shape is barely a pinprick.
A leviathan-back surfacing at the far sea-channel, matchstick-wide and horizon-long, the dark wet curve visible for a breath before the deep water closes again.
Pixel-tall sphinx-silhouette on the distant cliff promontory, motionless and barely distinguishable from the rock itself, readable only by the slight asymmetry of its seated outline.
A crane-formation of eleven ant-sized V-shapes overhead, their wing-beats synchronized into a single slow pulse, crossing the pale morning sky from east to far west.
Dire-bear on the far ridge, a single matchstick-dark shape that pauses at the crest, turns its head once, and drops below the tree-line before any detail resolves.
A faerie-cluster hovering at the deep-distance garden wall, their collective glow a faint smudge of blue-white too small to separate into individual lights from here.
Wyvern silhouette banking over the far mountain shoulder, pixel-tall and two-winged, its barbed tail readable in outline only when it crosses the last pale strip of sky.
Ant-sized bison-thunder crossing the midground valley floor, the herd's collective dark mass rolling like a slow bruise across the pale winter grass toward the river.
A spirit-fox at the forest edge in deep distance, matchstick-white and briefly luminous, its shape visible for only a moment before the shadow-line of the pines absorbs it.
Dolphin-pod cresting at the far cove, three pinprick arcs rising and falling in loose sequence, their motion the only thing separating them from the glittering wave-noise below.
A lone giant on the horizon plain, matchstick-tall and barely upright-readable, its silhouette distinguished from a standing stone only by the slow shift of its weight.
Merfolk silhouette at the deep-distance reef-break, ant-sized and half-submerged, their shapes visible only in the brief still moment between one wave-crest and the next.
